record.paper_title: Control of multi-agent systems: Results, open problems, and applications
record.context_brief: Flow-level control for measure differential equations
record.original_question: Let M be a manifold, let P(M) be the space of probability measures on M, and let P(TM) be the space of probability measures on the tangent bundle TM. A probability vector field is a map V: P(M) -> P(TM) satisfying pi_# V(mu) = mu, where pi: TM -> M is the bundle projection and # denotes push-forward of measures. For the measure differential equation mu_dot = V[mu], interpreted weakly by testing against functions f on M, can one study control properties at the level of the flows generated by the equation, rather than at the level of individual solutions, in the non-variational setting where probability vector fields have only an abelian monoid structure and not a Lie algebra structure?

evidence.quote: control properties at the level of the flows

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a smooth manifold, let $\mathcal{P}(M)$ denote the space of Borel probability measures on $M$, and let $\mathcal{P}(TM)$ denote the space of Borel probability measures on the tangent bundle $TM$, with bundle projection $\pi: TM \to M$. A probability vector field on $M$ is a map $V: \mathcal{P}(M) \to \mathcal{P}(TM)$ satisfying the marginal condition $\pi_{\#} V(\mu) = \mu$ for every $\mu \in \mathcal{P}(M)$, where $\#$ denotes push-forward of measures. Consider the measure differential equation
$$\dot\mu_t = V[\mu_t],$$
interpreted in the weak sense: for every test function $f \in C^1_c(M)$,
$$\frac{d}{dt}\int_M f\,d\mu_t = \int_{TM} \langle df(x), v\rangle\, dV(\mu_t)(x,v).$$
The set of probability vector fields carries a natural abelian monoid structure (e.g. fiberwise convolution of distributions on $TM$) but, in general, no Lie algebra structure, and the flow generated by such an equation need not arise from a variational (Wasserstein gradient flow) principle.

Develop a theory of controllability for the measure differential equation $\dot\mu_t = V[\mu_t]$ formulated at the level of the flows generated on $\mathcal{P}(M)$, rather than at the level of individual trajectories, in this non-variational setting where only the abelian monoid structure on probability vector fields is available. In particular, identify appropriate notions of accessibility, reachable set, and orbit on $\mathcal{P}(M)$, and provide structural conditions on a family $\{V_\alpha\}$ of probability vector fields that guarantee controllability of the induced flows.
artifact.status_search_result: The framework of measure differential equations driven by probability vector fields is recent and active; existence/uniqueness and (in some cases) dissipative/variational evolution semigroups in Wasserstein spaces have been developed, but no published work provides a controllability theory at the flow level for the non-variational case where only an abelian monoid structure (and no Lie bracket) is available. The question is posed explicitly as an open direction.

status_evidence.title: Measure Differential Equations
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces probability vector fields and measure differential equations with weak solutions, existence and uniqueness results.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes the analytic foundations but does not address flow-level controllability.

status_evidence.title: Dissipative probability vector fields and generation of evolution semigroups in Wasserstein spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Develops generation of evolution semigroups for dissipative probability vector fields in Wasserstein spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Treats dynamics/well-posedness but not control of flows in the non-variational abelian monoid setting.

status_evidence.title: Measure dynamics with Probability Vector Fields and sources
status_evidence.snippet: Notes that MDEs correspond to a monoid morphism mapping sums of vector fields to fiber convolution of probability vector fields.
status_evidence.claim: Confirms only an abelian monoid (not Lie algebra) structure is generally available.
